what: Guardant Health makes blood tests for cancer. Its tests detect tumour DNA circulating in blood, used to choose treatments, monitor for recurrence after surgery, and screen for colorectal cancer.
customers: Oncologists and hospitals ordering tests, pharmaceutical companies using its tests in trials, and screening patients through their doctors.
money: Guardant360 therapy selection and Reveal recurrence monitoring
moat: Years of clinical evidence and insurer coverage decisions for blood-based tumour testing, plus the regulatory approval for a blood screening test that competitors do not have.
risks: It makes a large operating loss
Reimbursement decisions determine whether tests get paid for
Blood-based colorectal screening is less sensitive than colonoscopy, which affects guidelines
Debt of about $1.7 billion against $1 billion of cash
opportunities: Revenue grew about 33% last year and about 30% a year over three years
Gross margin of 64% means volume growth converts to profit over time
Colorectal screening by blood test could reach millions who avoid colonoscopy
watch: Shield screening test volumes and gross margin improvement.
